key_insight: A neural-network interatomic potential trained with MatterSim-guided sampling and DFT fine-tuning can predict elastic and thermal trends in V-Ti-Cr alloys, showing that Cr stiffens while Ti softens the material.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable atomistic modeling route for designing fusion-relevant vanadium alloys with tunable stiffness and temperature-dependent mechanical performance.
method: Two-stage dataset generation: broad configuration sampling with MatterSim, then fine-tuning to VASP DFT data.
Trained a descriptor-based DeepMD-DPA1 potential for the V-Ti-Cr system.
Used large-cell LAMMPS simulations to compute elastic moduli and melting behavior across compositions and temperatures.
evidence_signal: The model reports RMSEs of 9.2 meV/atom for energies and 0.23 eV/angstrom for force components, and reproduces pure V melting near 1950 K.
watch_item: Predictions depend on the coverage and transferability of the training data, so compositions or temperatures outside the sampled V-Ti-Cr space may be less reliable.
paper_title: Mechanical properties of V-4Ti-4Cr alloy from molecular dynamics with a neural-network potential
